estimation_procedure.description: A pooled cross-sectional/time-series regression of one-year-ahead operating cash flow on seven current-period terms is reported in Table 3 Panel A. The paper says its findings to that point pool observations over time and across firms; separate-by-year Equation (12) fits are a later robustness check and are excluded. No observations are repeated by firm, industry, or year in the selected fit.

evidence.quote: The findings thus far are based on pooling observations over time and across firms.
Thus, as a robustness check, we estimate equation (12) separately by year.

All variables are deflated by the average book value of total assets (#6).

columns: Current through current and six lags (k=0–6)

models.sample_description: Compustat annual industrial and research-file observations for 1987–1996 predicting cash flow in 1988–1997. Table 2 reports k=0, 1, and 2 fits at n=10,164; k=3 at n=9,250; k=4 at n=8,491; k=5 at n=7,821; and k=6 at n=7,213. The underlying primary screen excludes financial-services firms (SIC 6000–6999), sales below $10 million, share price below $1, EARN or CF in the extreme upper/lower 1% of their distributions, and absolute studentized residuals above 3; the residual-generating regression is not identified.

fixed_effects.details: Table 2 does not report fixed-effect families. Later discussion that results are pooled across firms and time does not establish explicit fixed-effect absence.

standard_errors.details: Table 2 reports coefficient t-statistics but does not identify a standard-error correction or clustering dimension.

evidence.quote: t-statistic
Intercept

estimation_procedure.description: Equation (11) is repeatedly estimated for k=0,…,6, where each fit includes current EARN and lags through t−k. The sample count varies with k: n=10,164 for k=0–2, 9,250 for k=3, 8,491 for k=4, 7,821 for k=5, and 7,213 for k=6. The paper uses up to six lags to match Equation (12)’s seven explanatory terms when comparing predictive ability.

evidence.quote: k ranges from 0 to 6.

We use up to six lags of earnings because this results in the same number of explanatory variables in equation (11) as in the accrual components equation (12), ensuring that any difference in explanatory power is not attributable solely to the number of explanatory variables.
